name: John Kinzie's engagés, at the lodging house by his
head: kinzie_boatman_1812

present_on_scene_date.note: Each person's own card says how their presence on 14 August is known.

associated_with.note: Wau-Bun's lodging house 'for the Frenchmen' beside the Kinzie house; which men slept there is not said.

not_in_this_household.note: Everyone the T-3463..T-3467 day readings put in this household is on the card (liberty L-1812-town-days-3463).

persons.name: The Kinzie boatman, name not recorded

present_on_scene_date.note: The boatmen of the 15th (Wau-Bun; Currey). No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Currey and Kirkland count "a boatman" in the boat of 15 August; Wau-Bun says "the boatmen". French Canadian or Métis, as the Kinzie engagés were (Andreas p. 73: "the Canadian voyageurs in the service of Mr. Kinzie"; Kirkland app. D). No name. In the town from 1812-05-01 to 1812-08-18: In the boat on 15 August and with the family to St Joseph on the 18th. Engagés went out to the wintering grounds in the fall (Wau-Bun ch. XVIII, of 1811) and came in with the furs in spring; so from November to April they are taken to be away at an outpost, and back at Chicago from May. Both dates are ours.

evidence.locator: ch. XIX, PG 51737 (1856 text as reprinted in the 1901 Caxton Club edition) lines 6135-6137
evidence.quote: a clerk of Mr. Kinzie's, two servants and the boatmen, besides the two Indians who acted as their protectors
two servants, a boatman, and the two Indians who had brought the message from Topenebe
the Canadian voyageurs in the service of Mr. Kinzie were about the only white men who had occasion to visit Chicago

evidence.locator: ch. XVII, PG 51737 (1856 text as reprinted in the 1901 Caxton Club edition) lines 5141-5142
evidence.quote: establishment--dairy, bake-house, lodging-house for the Frenchmen, and stables.
evidence.claim: the dairy, bake-house, lodging-house for the Frenchmen and stables (as in 1831)

evidence.quote: In the out-buildings were accommodated dairy, baking-ovens, stables and rooms for "the Frenchmen," the Canadian engages
evidence.claim: the outbuildings: dairy, ovens, stables, rooms for the engagés

evidence.locator: ch. XVII, PG 51737 (1856 text as reprinted in the 1901 Caxton Club edition) lines 5457-5458
evidence.quote: rations of one quart of lyed corn, and two ounces of tallow per diem

evidence.locator: ch. XVII, PG 51737 (1856 text as reprinted in the 1901 Caxton Club edition) lines 5492-5494
evidence.quote: to toil by day, and laugh, joke, sing, and tell stories when the evening hour brought rest and liberty
